labels: Only a small fraction at once
scenes.narration: Just... not all at the same time. At any moment, only a small fraction of your neurons is firing. And that's on purpose.
scenes.image_prompt: the brain city at night with only a few calm lights glowing in different districts, the rest resting in soft blue darkness

scenes.narration: Right now, your eyes, ears and skin are sending your brain a flood of information. Millions of signals, every single second!
scenes.image_prompt: a waterfall of glowing light particles pouring from an eye, an ear and a hand into a calm brain-shaped lake

gfx.caption: bits per second, from your eyes alone (estimate)

scenes.narration: Fewer than a hundred cases have been studied. And many of them say it's not only a gift. Because the bad memories stay sharp too.
scenes.image_prompt: a glass jar of glowing memories, mostly warm golden lights but a few dark stormy ones swirling just as bright
a stopwatch made of light floating over a quiet night race track

scenes.narration: And still, it takes you about a quarter of a second to react. See the ball... move your hand.
scenes.image_prompt: a tennis ball frozen in mid-air in front of a racket, a glowing timer ring around it showing a quarter

scenes.narration: Even your sense of now is a little late! Your brain takes a fraction of a second to build each moment, then quietly edits it, so sound and sight feel perfectly in sync.
scenes.image_prompt: a film editor's desk made of light, two glowing strips of sound and picture sliding into place together, a small clock ticking softly

scenes.narration: Your brain works best in a narrow temperature range. A few degrees too warm, and thinking gets foggy. Push it further... and it becomes dangerous.
scenes.image_prompt: a glowing thermometer standing next to a brain, the safe zone glowing teal and the top glowing warning amber
a small sprout growing out of a glowing book at dawn

scenes.narration: Even while you sleep, your brain replays the day and keeps what matters. So a well-rested brain is already closer to one hundred percent than a tired one.
scenes.image_prompt: a peaceful bedroom at night, a dreamy glowing replay of the day drifting above the bed like constellations, a person sleeping peacefully
a glowing comic-style lightning bolt inside a glass sphere under the stars

scenes.narration: Real neuroscience has found no sign of any of that. Your brain can't send thoughts through the air. Or bend a spoon.
scenes.image_prompt: a spoon floating in front of a glowing brain, a big friendly teal cross mark next to it

scenes.narration: And if every neuron really fired at once? We actually know what that looks like. It's called a seizure. Not genius... chaos.
scenes.image_prompt: the brain city lights flickering wildly and shorting out, lightning between the districts, then darkness

scenes.narration: Some researchers think that in flow, the parts of your brain that judge and second-guess... quiet down. Not more brain. Less noise.
scenes.image_prompt: the brain city at night with the busy front district dimming calmly while one bright path glows steadily through it

scenes.narration: And feeling? It can write a poem about rain. But as far as we can tell, it has never smelled rain. That round... stays open.
scenes.image_prompt: the AI titan (a towering figure of dark glass panels with glowing amber circuit lines and calm amber eyes) gently drawing flowing ribbons of amber light in the air while real rain falls outside a large window behind it

scenes.narration: Final score: three to three. A tie! And the most interesting result came from chess.
scenes.image_prompt: a holographic tournament board in a big arena showing two glowing score bars almost equal, confetti of light, no numbers, no writing

scenes.narration: So your brain doesn't need to run at one hundred percent. It needs the right lights on at the right time. Good sleep. Real challenges. A little less noise.
scenes.image_prompt: the brain night city calm and beautiful, the right districts glowing warmly, a soft sunrise beginning on the horizon

scenes.narration: The question isn't who wins. It's what you'll build. See you on the next orbit.
scenes.image_prompt: a small green glass planet with a glowing orbit ring floating in space at sunrise, tiny forests and a glass city on it
